background.name: Fey-Touched

_.special: One token (your choice) representing your relation to the fey

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: You can speak, read, and write {@language Sylvan}

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: One token (your choice) representing your relation to the fey, {@item fine clothes|PHB|fine clothing}, and 10gp.

entries: You have, in one way or another, been touched by the fey. You might have a friendly relationship with them, and they treat your words as higher than those of other mortals, or you may have accidentally given your name to one of them in your youth, or you may a spark of their magic from far back in your bloodline. Those who find their paths speckled with fey magic tend to be specially in tune with the nature around them, and have a natural talent towards convincing others to see their point of view.

background.name: Spirit of the Wild

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: You can speak, read, and write one language of your choosing.

entries: You have been touched by wild magic, the force of chaos that underlies creation. In one way or another, this has followed you throughout your life, whether that be granting you a special affinity towards magic, or causing horrible things to follow in your wake. This has led you to wander from place to place, with no permanent residence to call home. Through this, your body and mind have gained an ability to weather the elements, as well as survive them, and you have picked up knowledge of other cultures from your travels.

race.name: Fey-Touched Tiefling
entries: As a Fey-Touched Tiefling, you gain the following traits:

entries.name: Age
entries: Fey-Touched tieflings tend to live longer than other variants of tiefling, likely due to the magic they carry. On average, they live to around 150 years.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write {@language Common} and {@language Sylvan}.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: Thanks to your fey heritage, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} within 60 feet of you as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light}, and in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||darkness} as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light}. You can't discern colors in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||darkness}, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition charmed} condition on yourself.

entries.name: Legacy of the Fey
entries: Your fey ancestry has granted you magical abilities. You know the {@spell Dancing Lights} and {@spell Prestidigitation} cantrips. When you reach 3rd level, you can cast the {@spell Disguise Self} spell as a 2nd-level spell once with this trait. When you reach 5th level, you can cast the {@spell Crown of Madness} spell once with this trait. Once you cast {@spell Disguise Self} or {@spell Crown of Madness} with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest.You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when you cast them with this trait (choose when you select this species).

race.name: Wild Magic Tiefling
entries: As a Wild Magic Tiefling, you gain the following traits:

entries.name: Age
entries: Wild magic tieflings mature at the same rate as {@race human||humans}, but live a bit longer.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write {@language Common} and {@language Primordial}.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: Thanks to your magical heritage, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} within 60 feet of you as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light}, and in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||darkness} as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light}. You can't discern colors in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||darkness}, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Chaotic Resilience
entries: The pure chaos that spawned you has granted you an ever-shifting defense against elemental magic. After each long rest, roll a d6 on the Chaotic Resilience Table. Depending on the result, you have resistance to one of six damage types:

entries.name: Legacy of Chaos
entries: The chaos you emerged from has granted you abilities specific to your kind. You know the {@spell Elementalism|XPHB} and {@spell Thaumaturgy} cantrips. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the {@spell Chromatic Orb} spell at 2nd level with this trait, without requiring a material component. Starting at 5th level, you can also cast the {@spell Shatter} spell with this trait, without requiring a material component. Once you cast {@spell Chromatic Orb} or {@spell Shatter} with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when you cast them with this trait (choose when you select this species).
{@spell Elementalism|XPHB} is a 5.5e spell. If you don't want to use any 5.5e content, you can replace it with the {@spell Druidcraft} cantrip.

raceFluff.name: Fey-Touched Tiefling
entries: Rather than being born of the demonic, tieflings of this variant have had their bloodline touched by the magic of the Feywild. Their bodies have been altered by this magic from a normal human's appearance. They might have cloven feet, wings that cannot lift their body weight, or have brightly colored skin.

raceFluff.name: Wild Magic Tiefling
entries: Instead of being born of the demonic, these tieflings were touched by or spawned into being by wild magic itself. Consequently, their form is wild magic's best attempt at creating a mortal; their body isn't quite what it should be. They might be missing a limb, have one leg shorter than the other, or not have eyes.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Carrion

entries: Decay exists as an extant form of life.

Like all druids, you are deeply in tune with nature and its workings. However, you understand that in order for life to flourish, some of those belonging to it must rot. You have dedicated yourself to ensuring that this part of the cycle of life is fulfilled sufficiently to maintain balance.
Those who dedicate themselves to the Circle of Carrion wield powerful necrotic spells, and bond themselves to other creatures in the ecosystem who fulfill the same purpose.

subclassFeature.name: Circle Spells
entries: {@i 2nd-level Circle of Carrion feature}
Your magic grants you an innate knowledge of life and death, granting you access to additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Carrion Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

subclassFeature.name: Friend of the Scavengers
entries: {@i 2nd-level Circle of Carrion feature}

Your magical specialties have led you to befriend the scavengers and carrion eaters in the ecosystem. Beginning at 2nd level, you can summon beast-type creatures who share your goal of continuing the cycle of life. These must be singular creatures, not swarms, and approved by your GM. These creatures act independently of you, but always obey your commands. You can do this twice per long rest, with scavengers and carrion eaters of up to CR 1.

While they are summoned, you and the creature can understand each other's speech. Additionally, you can take an action to see through its eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining the benefits of any special senses that the creature has. During this time, you are {@condition deafened||deaf} and {@condition blinded||blind} with regard to your own senses.

During combat, your summoned creature rolls its own initiative and acts on its own turn. If they have an action on their stat block that allows them to attack, they can attack hostile creatures. If the animal drops to 0 hit points during combat, you can use your action to magically restore the creature by sacrificing an amount of HP equal to at least half its max HP, with the creature being revived with the amount of hit points you sacrificed, or to magically sap the remaining life energy from its body, returning its carcass to the earth and regaining an amount of HP equal to half the creature's max HP. These creatures can benefit from healing spells such as {@spell Cure Wounds}.
The summoning of this creature lasts for a number of hours equal to half your druid level.
This ability scales as you level up. Please refer to the Friend of the Scavengers Table for more information.
Examples of such creatures you could summon are ravens, vultures, polar bears, sharks, lions, and coyotes.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Decay
entries: {@i 6th-level Circle of Carrion feature}

The energy of death and rot follows you. Plant life around you slowly withers and dies, and when you will it, it can grow powerful enough to affect larger creatures. You gain resistance to necrotic and poison damage. Additionally, as an action, you can summon the rot you radiate onto hostile creatures within 15 feet of you, decreasing their AC by 2. A creature can only be affected by this once per combat. The penalty to AC increases to 3 at 10th level, 4 at 14th level, and 5 at 18th level.

subclassFeature.name: Lord of the Carrion Eaters
entries: {@i 10th-level Circle of Carrion feature}

The scavengers grow fonder of you. Beginning at 10th level, you can summon multiple creatures using your {@subclassFeature Friend of the Scavengers|Druid|PHB|Carrion|GlensGrimoireOfMayhem|2} ability. Their CR must add up to the maximum CR you are able to summon, and you can summon a number of creatures up to twice the maximum CR you are able to summon.

subclassFeature.name: Purveyor of Rot
entries: {@i 14th-level Circle of Carrion feature}

The decay that follows you has grown stronger. You gain immunity to necrotic and poison damage. Additionally, your Aura of Decay action increases to a radius of 30 feet and you use its action, and in addition to the AC penalty, the creatures targeted also make a Constitution saving throw. If they fail the saving throw, they take {@damage 2d8} necrotic damage, and take it again at the beginning of each of their turns. At the end of the creature's turn, they can remake the Constitution saving throw. On a success, the effect ends.
At 18th level, the necrotic damage increases to {@damage 3d8}.

spell.name: Meteor Beam

components.m: a small piece of a meteorite

entries: You summon forth the power of space to obliterate your foes. You gather cosmic power around yourself, and fire a beam of pure spatial matter 100 feet long and 5 feet wide which blasts out from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 4d6} bludgeoning damage and {@damage 4d6} radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the bludgeoning or the radiant damage (your choice) increases by {@scaledamage 4d6|4-9|1d6} for each slot level above 4th.
